brief.headline: Move from immediate payment to 30-day credit to free ₹44.91 L in working capital — our strongest lever against a small-margin, cash-stretched supplier.

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark laminate price to the BOPET film import unit value and ask for a 6.7% reduction in exchange for faster payment than their current 63-day payables.
priceAsk.target: 171.60 ₹/kg BOPET film import unit value as the substrate floor
priceAsk.basis: They stretch their own suppliers to 63d vs 6d peer median, yet we pay on delivery. Their borrowing cost is 6.7%, so paying them faster than market is worth that rate to them — trade speed for price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Shift from Immediate payment to standard 30-day credit, with a stepped offer of 15 days as a fallback.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹44.91 L freed at 30 days; ₹22.45 L at 15 days

brief.financialLeverage: Tetrapak earns a 5.4% net margin vs 10.2% peer median — materially below par, so deep price cuts are difficult. They carry 1.09x debt-to-equity and a 75d cash-conversion cycle vs 30d peer median, meaning they value cash flow. We represent 0.12% of their ₹4491.70 Cr revenue, so standalone leverage is low. However, their Altman Z-score of 2.15 puts them in the grey zone, and they flag severe legal case(s), so continuity is a watch — approach payment terms and modest price adjustments, not a hard squeeze.

evidence.point: They earn half the peer margin, so price flexibility is limited
They stretch their own suppliers far past the market norm
Their cash cycle is more than twice the peer median, so they value faster payment
We are a rounding error in their book
evidence.figure: ₹5.46 Cr spend is 0.12% of ₹4491.70 Cr revenue

evidence.point: Geared balance sheet — debt is a continuity and cash-flow watch
Financial distress signal — not safe, not crisis

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volume — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets, health score B (64/100), ₹2611.64 Cr revenue.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant covering both film substrate and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale, ₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health C (54/100).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter for pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second-source fit, ₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D (31/100).

risks: Below-peer 5.4% margin means limited room for deep price cuts — push too hard and they walk or cut corners.
Altman Z of 2.15 (grey zone) and severe legal case(s) flag continuity risk — qualify a second source before pressing aggressively.
We are 0.12% of their revenue, so standalone leverage is minimal — bundle volume commitments or multi-year terms to gain negotiating weight.
22% goods-receipt reversal rate signals quality or paperwork issues — resolve before it costs us more in disruption and rework.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to standard 30-day payment terms and benchmark laminate pricing to the BOPET substrate import line of 171.60 ₹/kg — in return, we'll commit volume and pay you faster than the market median of 6 days, which should be worth your 6.7% borrowing cost.
